title: Henselian property of the existing ind-etale closed lift
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $\overline C$ an ind-etale $A/I$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $C=H_A(\overline C)$ and $\epsilon:C\to\overline C$ be the colimit algebra and specified map constructed in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], and let $IC$ be the ideal generated by the image of $I$. Then $(C,IC)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Definition 2.2.10 and Lemma 2.2.12; Section 6.1, Lemma 6.1.1 and the henselian-pair description in the proof of Lemma 6.1.2

proof.text: Put $J=IC$ and write $\rho:C\to C/J$ for the quotient map. The small category $\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ is filtered by [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered]. Its terms are etale $A$-algebras of finite presentation and its colimit is $C$ by [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]; thus $C/A$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction] the specified reduction map $\theta:C/J\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline C$ is an isomorphism and $\theta\rho=\epsilon$.

source.place: Tag 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale): the filtered construction and its specified closed-fibre isomorphism

proof.text: To verify the etale-section lifting hypothesis, fix any etale ring map $u:C\to E$ and any $C$-algebra map $\sigma:E\to C/J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], $E$ is finitely presented over $C$. The one-object constant presentation makes $E/C$ ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Composition stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], applied to $A\to C\xrightarrow{u}E$, now makes $E$ an ind-etale $A$-algebra. No finiteness assumption on $A$ or $I$ is used.

source.place: Definition 2.2.1(5) and Proposition 2.3.3(4), composition of ind-etale maps

proof.text: Set $q=\theta\circ\sigma:E\to\overline C$. Since $\sigma$ is $C$-linear, $qu=\theta\rho=\epsilon$. In particular $q$ annihilates the ideal $IE$ generated by the image of $I$, and induces an $A/I$-algebra map $\overline q:E/IE\to\overline C$, given by $[e]\mapsto q(e)$. Apply the bijection in [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction] with $D=E$. Surjectivity gives an $A$-algebra map $\tau:E\to C$ corresponding to $\overline q$. The formula in that node, evaluated on every quotient representative $[e]$, says precisely $\epsilon\tau=q$.

The two $A$-algebra maps $\tau u,\operatorname{id}_C:C\to C$ satisfy $\epsilon\tau u=qu=\epsilon$. Apply injectivity of the same bijection [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction], now with $D=C$, which is ind-etale over $A$ by step 1. Their corresponding maps $C/IC\to\overline C$ agree on all classes $[c]$, since their composites with $\epsilon$ agree; hence $\tau u=\operatorname{id}_C$. Thus $\tau$ is a $C$-algebra map. Moreover $\theta\rho\tau=\epsilon\tau=q=\theta\sigma$, so injectivity of the specified isomorphism $\theta$ from step 1 gives $\rho\tau=\sigma$. This is the required lift of the given section on the closed fibre.

source.place: Tag 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale), injectivity of the adjunction bijection, with source C; elementary cancellation of the specified reduction isomorphism

proof.text: The preceding construction works for every etale $C$-algebra $E$ and every $C$-algebra map $E\to C/J$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-lifting-henselian-pair], applied with its ring $A=C$ and ideal $I=J$, proves that $(C,J)$ is henselian: every idempotent of $F/JF$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $F$ for every finite $C$-algebra $F$. Since $J=IC$, this is the stated conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Definition 2.2.10 and Lemma 2.2.12; the henselian-pair assertion used in Lemma 6.1.2 is proved explicitly from the existing adjunction via Stacks Tag 09XI (2) implies (3).

It also matches Stacks proetale.tex Tag 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale) and the adjunction trick near line 4827 (C->C_g->C/IC gives a C-algebra map), which steps 3-4 generalize. Steps: step 1 (elementary) uses the filteredness, colimit-definition and reduction-iso statements, giving C ind-étale and theta∘rho=epsilon. Step 2: Mathlib leaf clause (1) gives E finitely presented; the one-object presentation plus composition stability give E ind-étale over A. Step 3: q=theta∘sigma satisfies q∘u=epsilon and kills IE; surjectivity of the adjunction at D=E gives tau with epsilon∘tau=q. Step 4: injectivity at D=C gives tau∘u=id, and injectivity of theta gives rho∘tau=sigma.
